topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Hallmarks of Cancer Framework
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the learning objectives, tumor progression model, and the conceptual framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Proliferative Signaling and Growth Control Pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations in receptor tyrosine kinase and Wnt signaling cascades drive autonomous cell proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation Block in Tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer cells disrupt normal terminal differentiation in both hematopoietic malignancies and colonic epithelia.

topics.label: Evasion of Apoptosis and the p53 Pathway
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the molecular mechanisms and regulatory proteins by which cancer cells suppress programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative Immortality, Telomeres, and Senescence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the mechanisms of telomere shortening, senescence fail-safes, and how cancer cells achieve immortality by activating telomerase.

topics.label: Altered Cellular Metabolism and Metabolic Rewiring
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the transition to complex cancer hallmarks and the metabolic reprogramming characterized by aerobic glycolysis and oncometabolite-driven epigenetic changes.

topics.label: Tumor Angiogenesis and Neovascularization
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses the angiogenic switch and the balance of signals required to stimulate new blood vessel growth for tumor survival.

topics.label: Invasion, Metastasis, and Clonal Dissemination
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyse the multi-step metastatic cascade, systemic spread via the circulation, and the genomic features underlying secondary site colonization.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Practical Guidance
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer wraps up the session by referencing advanced hallmark literature, reiterating core learning objectives, and inviting questions.
